We need count of methyl groups in the molecule. But we don't have the molecule given. Possibly the sample is the compound at hand, which we can get NMR spectra to infer methyl groups. We need to determine number of methyl groups (CH3) in the unknown molecule. We can use proton NMR to see signals for methyl (singlet, doublet, etc). Also carbon NMR for methyl carbons (~10-30 ppm). Could also use HSQC to correlate.

We need to decide which measurement to perform. Since we just need count, maybe proton NMR is enough: count number of distinct methyl signals? But overlapping may be ambiguous. Could also use carbon NMR to count number of methyl carbons. That may be more straightforward: each methyl carbon appears around 10-30 ppm. So we can get carbon NMR and count peaks in that region.

Thus we should call carbon_nmr_spectra tool.
